name: Is it safe to set the password on PDFree's website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The entire encryption process runs in your browser using pdf-lib. Your password and document are never transmitted to any server — PDFree literally cannot see them.

name: Does PDFree store or log my files after processing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. PDFree runs entirely in your browser — there is no backend server that receives your files. Because nothing is uploaded, nothing can be stored, logged, or retained. Your document exists only in your browser's memory for the duration of the session and is cleared when you close the tab.

name: What encryption standard does PDFree use?

acceptedAnswer.text: PDFree uses AES-256 encryption, the same standard used by banks and government systems.

name: Can I set separate passwords for opening and editing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can set an owner password (for editing/printing restrictions) separately from a user password (for opening the file).
AES-256 is practically uncrackable by brute force. Use a strong, unique password for best security.

name: Will the password-protected PDF open in Adobe Reader?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. PDFree produces standard-compliant encrypted PDFs that open in Adobe Acrobat, Adobe Reader, macOS Preview, and all modern PDF viewers.

name: Can I remove the password from a protected PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — upload the encrypted PDF, enter the current password, leave the new password field empty, and save. This produces an unprotected version of the file.
